observations: The new linearity bound has less room on this node than the implementer's twenty runs showed. In my twenty isolated pairs at the head the ratio reached 3.96x and 3.77x on the 49-marker shape (2 of 20 over the 3.5x bound), 0.91-3.50x on the 8,000 items and 1.44-2.68x on the brackets. The excursions come from the half write, not the body: the marker halves ranged 250-597 ms while the bodies stayed 643-1,247. My pairs do not carry the row's own warming write for that shape, which is the likeliest reason the implementer's twenty runs stayed at 1.22-3.11x, so this is a margin to know about rather than a defect - but on a node where the half can halve, a 3.5x bound is one jitter away from red.

Firefox's page-parsed row is over the main-thread bound on this pod at both revisions. '49 list markers on one line then blank lines, just under the worker's threshold' measured 971 ms in the sweep and 794, 1185, 1524, 982 ms in four repeats at the head - and 1133, 1023, 1169, 1059 ms, 4 of 4 over, at 94f1caba. So the head is better than the defective head on the very row that reds, and the row's absolute gap bound belongs to CI for the same reason the write row's does. This pod is not the one it was in round 3, where the same row read 402 ms in Firefox: the volume and the harness have been rebuilt twice since, browsers included.

Every checkout this round was made with git archive into $TMPDIR and built there (bun install, contracts, build:web), so the shared workspace was never touched by a measurement, and each role's Postgres lane is its own (LEGION_ROLE=tester; I had to create dispatch_tester_e2e once, which setup.sh does not).
